title: Create a reproducible Python workspace
objective: Create an isolated project environment, install only project dependencies, and prove that the same project can be opened from a terminal and VS Code.
deliverable: A working virtual environment and a saved environment manifest (requirements.txt).
prerequisites: Academy folder extracted to a writable local directory

commands: python -m pip install pandas numpy matplotlib
python -c 'import pandas, numpy, matplotlib; print(pandas.__version__, numpy.__version__, matplotlib.__version__)'
python -m pip install pandas numpy matplotlib
python -c "import pandas, numpy, matplotlib; print(pandas.__version__, numpy.__version__, matplotlib.__version__)"

steps: Open the academy root folder in VS Code, not an individual script file.
Run the commands for your operating system in order. Do not mix Windows and Linux activation commands.
In VS Code, open the command palette and choose Python: Select Interpreter. Select the interpreter inside the academy root's .venv directory.
Create a file named environment_check.py containing: `import sys, pandas, numpy, matplotlib; print(sys.executable); print(pandas.__version__)`. Run it using the selected interpreter.
Keep `.venv/` out of Git. Keep requirements.txt in the project so another machine can recreate the environment.
acceptance: The final import command exits without an exception.
The printed executable path points inside this Academy's .venv.
requirements.txt exists and lists pandas, numpy and matplotlib.
troubleshooting: Linux permission or externally-managed-environment error
Do not use sudo pip. Confirm the venv is active and the prompt/path points to .venv.
Fish reports unknown command for activation
Use `source .venv/bin/activate.fish`; the Bash activation file is not for Fish.
PowerShell blocks Activate.ps1
Use the current-user policy only if permitted by your organisation: `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned`; otherwise run `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip ...` without activation.
VS Code imports fail while terminal works
Select the same .venv interpreter in VS Code and restart the notebook/kernel.
precautions: Do not install packages into Arch's system Python with sudo pip.
Do not commit .venv, secrets, patient data or credentials.
The Windows commands are authored for PowerShell; they have not been executed on a Windows host as part of this release.
portfolio: Record Python version, package versions and a short README setup section. This is evidence of reproducible environment management.

title: Profile and validate a healthcare CSV with pandas
objective: Inspect row grain, schema, missingness, duplicate keys, invalid categories and date validity before analysis.
deliverable: A profiling report and validation log for the synthetic encounter dataset.
prerequisites: Use only the synthetic Academy dataset
steps: Read `projects/v03_python_analysis/cleaning_rules.md` before executing transformations.
Open `projects/v03_python_analysis/data_quality_pipeline.py`; identify input path, declared key, required columns, validation rules and output directory.
Run the script from the Academy root so relative paths resolve consistently.
Inspect every generated report in `projects/v03_python_analysis/reports/`. Compare source row count with output row count; investigate every removed or flagged row.
Add a short QA note describing which checks passed, which failed, and whether each issue was corrected, excluded with justification, or retained.
acceptance: Script completes without a traceback.
The report includes source row count, missingness and duplicate/key checks.
No record is silently deleted solely because it is an outlier or has a missing value.
Every transformation is documented and the raw synthetic source remains unchanged.
troubleshooting: File not found
Run from the Academy root and verify the dataset and script paths. Do not move only the script out of its project.
Key duplicates detected
Determine whether the declared key is actually unique at the table's grain; repeated patients may be valid across encounters.
Missing values appear in output
Missingness is a finding, not automatically an error. Investigate patterns and meaning before imputation.
Pandas import error
Activate the .venv created in LAB-01 and install requirements from that environment.
precautions: A patient ID is not necessarily unique in an encounter- or order-level table.
Never interpret missing laboratory values as normal or zero.
Use synthetic records only; do not copy real hospital data into the Academy.
portfolio: Publish a de-identified methodology note and sample QA report using synthetic data. Include grain, key definition, validation rules and limitations.

title: Answer a prescribing question with SQL
objective: Translate a healthcare question into a reproducible query while preserving table grain and denominators.
deliverable: A saved SQL script and a metric-definition note.
prerequisites: SQLite database or CSV import capability
steps: Open `projects/v02_excel_sql_capstone/PROJECT_BRIEF.md` and identify the question, population, time period and unit of analysis.
Open `projects/v02_excel_sql_capstone/capstone_analysis_queries.sql` and read the table names and joins before running any query.
In DBeaver, create a local SQLite database. Import the workbook's prepared CSV/table data using the column types and keys in the project brief.
Run the queries individually. For each result, record the row grain and denominator. Compare a row count with a distinct-patient count to confirm they are not being confused.
Save your final query as `projects/v02_excel_sql_capstone/my_analysis.sql` (create this file) inside a private working copy of the project. Add comments explaining definitions and exclusions.
acceptance: Every query executes without syntax errors.
A distinct-patient count is not substituted for order/encounter row count.
Joins do not unintentionally multiply rows; compare pre- and post-join counts.
Every percentage or rate has an explicit numerator, denominator and period.
troubleshooting: No such table
Import the source tables first and check exact table names and case.
Unexpectedly inflated counts after join
Check one-to-many relationships and aggregate at the intended grain before joining.
NULL values disappear from a filter
Remember SQL three-valued logic; use `IS NULL` or `IS NOT NULL` explicitly.
Date filter excludes records
Inspect stored date format and use a consistent ISO date representation.
precautions: A prescription order does not prove dispensing, administration or patient adherence.
Avoid SELECT * for large production datasets; request only required columns.
Do not connect DBeaver to a live hospital database without written authorisation.
portfolio: Include the business question, SQL, data dictionary, metric definitions and a screenshot/export of synthetic output.

title: Run a defensible biostatistical cohort analysis
objective: Describe a synthetic cohort, quantify missingness and compare groups without overstating statistical or causal evidence.
deliverable: Reproducible analysis outputs and a one-page interpretation.
prerequisites: Read the V04 project brief and data dictionary
steps: Read the data dictionary and verify units, coding, missing-value conventions and cohort eligibility.
Run the analysis script from the Academy root or follow the project's README if its paths are relative to the project directory.
Inspect outputs in `projects/v04_biostatistics_research_project/outputs/`. Recalculate one summary manually from the CSV to check the code.
For any group comparison, state the outcome type, independent unit, assumptions, effect estimate and uncertainty. Do not select a test solely because it returns p < 0.05.
Write a results paragraph that separates descriptive findings from inferential findings and states that this synthetic exercise does not establish causality.
acceptance: The script validates required columns, unique synthetic patient identifiers and binary coding.
Group summaries and missingness metrics are present.
Interpretation names the unit of analysis and reports uncertainty where inferential statistics are used.
No causal claim is made from an observational comparison.
troubleshooting: Missing package
Install it inside .venv, not system Python.
Unexpected sample size
Check eligibility filters and missing-data exclusions; document the analysis denominator.
Statistically significant but tiny difference
Report magnitude and confidence interval; clinical importance is not determined by p-value alone.
Normality assumption questionable
Inspect distributions and use a method appropriate to design and data; do not treat a normality test as the sole decision rule.
precautions: Do not infer causality from unadjusted observational comparisons.
Do not run multiple tests and report only significant outcomes.
The synthetic cohort is for method practice, not clinical decision-making.
portfolio: Submit a reproducible report with cohort flow, descriptive table, missingness, effect estimates, confidence intervals, limitations and code.

title: Build a clinical pharmacy analytics data check
objective: Validate patient, encounter, laboratory and medication tables and produce safe descriptive summaries.
deliverable: A validation log and clinical-pharmacy summary report.
prerequisites: Read the V05 capstone README and project brief
steps: Inspect the data folder and read the data dictionary before joining tables.
State the grain of each table: patient, encounter, laboratory result or medication order.
Run the capstone script. Review `reports/outputs/` and the validation report.
Trace referential-integrity checks: every encounter patient should exist in the patient table; every child record should link to a valid parent where required.
Review medication and laboratory summaries. Confirm that an order is not labelled as administration and that missing test records are not labelled as normal.
acceptance: Key uniqueness and referential-integrity checks run.
Date chronology is checked and invalid chronology is reported.
Summary counts are explicitly labelled by their grain.
No laboratory-completion percentage is calculated without an expected-test denominator.
troubleshooting: Join duplicates patient rows
Aggregate child tables to patient/encounter grain before joining or preserve the one-to-many structure.
Date parsing fails
Inspect raw formats and parse explicitly; retain an invalid-date flag rather than silently coercing without reporting.
No test-completion denominator
Define eligible encounters and expected tests from a valid protocol before calculating completion.
Medication counts look too high
Check if counts represent orders, order lines, administrations or unique medicines.
precautions: Use only synthetic data in this project.
Do not make treatment recommendations from descriptive prescribing patterns alone.
Reference ranges depend on laboratory method, units, population and clinical context.
portfolio: Document the schema, table grains, validation rules, key metrics and clinical interpretation boundaries.

title: Create a lightweight ETL data mart
objective: Transform synthetic source tables into validated analytical marts with explicit metric definitions.
deliverable: CSV marts, SQL views and an ETL validation log.
prerequisites: At least 5 GB free disk space recommended; Docker optional
steps: Read the README and schema documentation. Identify source grain and intended mart grain.
Run the Python mart builder without Docker first; the local path is simpler and uses fewer resources.
Inspect each generated mart: row count, key uniqueness, nulls, date range and metric totals.
Open SQL definitions in DBeaver and compare SQL view results with the Python-generated mart. Explain any differences.
Only if needed, build and run the Docker image using the project's Dockerfile. Stop and remove the container after checking outputs.
acceptance: The Python ETL completes and writes expected mart outputs.
Mart grain and primary key are documented.
Validation checks cover required columns, uniqueness and referential integrity where relevant.
SQL and Python summaries reconcile or have documented, explained differences.
troubleshooting: Docker daemon unavailable
Skip Docker and use the documented local Python route; check `systemctl status docker` only if Docker is intended.
Out-of-memory or system becomes sluggish
Stop optional containers and use the local script; avoid running Superset, databases and notebooks concurrently on a 16 GB machine.
Marts have more rows than expected
Inspect join cardinality and source grain before changing aggregation.
SQL/Python totals differ
Check NULL handling, date boundaries, duplicate handling and grouping keys.
precautions: Docker is optional, not a prerequisite for learning ETL.
Do not expose database ports to the public network.
The generated readmission flag is synthetic teaching data, not a validated readmission measure.
portfolio: Deliver an architecture diagram, source-to-target mapping, SQL, ETL code, validation log and a data dictionary.

title: Publish a small dashboard safely
tools: CSV marts, Power BI Desktop on Windows OR Metabase/Superset on Linux
objective: Turn a validated mart into a decision-focused dashboard with clear definitions and appropriate visual encodings.
deliverable: A one-page dashboard plus metric dictionary and QA checklist.
prerequisites: Use only validated synthetic mart outputs

commands: # Open Power BI Desktop from the Start menu and import the validated CSV mart

steps: Choose one decision and one audience. Define no more than 4–6 primary metrics for the first page.
Write each metric definition before creating visuals: numerator, denominator, unit, time window, exclusions and refresh date.
Windows route: open Power BI Desktop, import the validated CSV mart, verify data types and create measures rather than relying on implicit sums.

Linux route: use a local spreadsheet for a lightweight chart, or deploy Metabase/Superset only if you have sufficient RAM and understand authentication, database access and network exposure. Power BI Desktop is not natively supported on Linux.
Use trend lines for time, bars for category comparisons and tables for exact values. Avoid 3D charts and truncated axes that exaggerate differences.
Validate every displayed total against the source mart and add a visible synthetic-data disclaimer.
acceptance: Each KPI has a documented definition and denominator.
Dashboard filters do not change the meaning of the metric silently.
At least one total is reconciled to source data.
The dashboard labels synthetic data and its refresh/as-of date.
troubleshooting: Power BI Desktop unavailable on Linux
This is expected; use an authorised Windows installation or Linux alternative. Do not assume Wine provides supported compatibility.
Chart totals differ from SQL
Check relationship cardinality, filter context, implicit aggregation and duplicate rows.
Dashboard too slow on local machine
Reduce data volume, close unused containers and use CSV extracts; avoid heavy services on 16 GB RAM.
Category order is wrong
Create an explicit sort column or sort by the intended measure.
precautions: Power BI Desktop is Windows-only; browser access to Power BI Service is not equivalent to Desktop modelling.
Do not publish identifiable patient data or dashboards to public workspaces.
Do not use a dashboard as a substitute for clinical review.
portfolio: Publish screenshots and a readme containing audience, decision, metric dictionary, data lineage, QA evidence and limitations.

title: Evaluate a clinical risk prediction model
objective: Evaluate a synthetic prediction model with a held-out test set, discrimination, calibration, threshold metrics and subgroup checks.
deliverable: A model evaluation report that communicates intended use and limitations.
prerequisites: Complete V04 statistics and V07 model evaluation chapters
steps: Read the project brief and inspect the synthetic cohort generation process. Identify target, prediction time and feature availability.
Run the model script and inspect metrics in `projects/v07_predictive_analytics_capstone/reports/`.
Check for leakage: no feature may contain information recorded after the prediction time or encode the outcome directly.
Interpret sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, ROC-AUC and calibration together. PPV/NPV depend on prevalence and the chosen threshold.
Review subgroup performance and uncertainty. Record limitations including synthetic data, sample size, dataset shift and absence of external validation.
acceptance: Train/test separation is documented and no test data are used for model selection.
Metrics are labelled with their evaluation split and threshold where relevant.
At least one calibration assessment and subgroup check is reported where data support it.
The report explicitly states that the model is not for clinical deployment or patient-level decisions.
troubleshooting: AUC looks implausibly high
Investigate target leakage, duplicated patients across splits and post-outcome variables.
PPV is low despite good sensitivity
Check outcome prevalence and threshold; PPV is prevalence-dependent.
Subgroup metric is unstable
Report subgroup sample sizes and uncertainty; do not rank groups on tiny denominators.
Scikit-learn import error
Install inside the active .venv and confirm VS Code uses that interpreter.
precautions: All cohort data are synthetic.
A model metric is not proof of clinical utility, fairness, safety or generalisability.
Do not deploy, prescribe, triage or make patient-level decisions using this educational model.
portfolio: Include model card, intended-use statement, split strategy, metric definitions, calibration, subgroup analysis, error analysis and explicit non-deployment disclaimer.
